shared_text:
The flight. A regional jet on an airline flight, on approach to a large airport. Visual conditions, daytime, gusty winds.

The crew. The first officer was the pilot flying and the captain the pilot monitoring.

What happened. The crew planned a visual approach backed up by the ILS. After several vectors the crew found unusual, the aircraft was turned in very close to the final approach fix and cleared for the ILS, keeping 170 knots to the fix. Because the turn to final would be almost over the fix, the first officer decided to intercept using the flight management system's course guidance, to reduce workload. Nearing the intercept, the first officer saw that this guidance was no longer displayed and the course would not be captured. As the aircraft passed through the final approach course, the first officer switched to localiser guidance and selected navigation mode. Knowing the descent must now be started manually, the first officer reset the selected altitude and selected vertical speed. The first officer then saw that the course had not been captured and the autopilot had reverted to roll mode. The captain had set the final approach speed of 143 knots, and was changing to the tower frequency and calling the before-landing check. The speed had been slowly decreasing in the gusty wind. As the first officer reached to disconnect the autopilot, the stick shaker activated briefly. The captain called "Speed", and the first officer took manual control and increased the speed.
safe_outcome: The first officer brought the aircraft back onto the final approach course and the visual approach path. The approach was stable before 1,000 ft, and the aircraft landed without further incident. There was no conflict with other traffic. No one was hurt and the aircraft was not damaged.
bad_outcome: Another aircraft was descending nearby. Both crews received TCAS resolution advisories and followed them, and the aircraft passed about 300 feet vertically and half a mile apart. A flight attendant on this aircraft was thrown against a galley cart during the manoeuvre and received a minor injury.

notes: Removed under rule 3: both 'Cause' and 'Suggestions' sections, including 'breakdown in visual scanning', 'over reliance on automation', 'momentarily overwhelmed by our automation usage', 'did not pay attention to speed as we should have' and 'when I should have been adding speed to my scan'. Kept as facts at the time: the crew's view that the vectors were unusual, the first officer's reason for choosing the flight management system guidance (workload), the switch to localiser guidance, the manual descent set-up, the roll-mode reversion, the captain's tasks at the time (speed set, frequency change, before-landing check, taken from the captain's account with the self-criticism removed), the decaying speed in gusty wind and the brief stick shaker. Moved to the safe ending (rule 5): the correction back onto the course and approach path, stable before 1,000 ft, and the landing. Removed under rule 6: the airport, the runway and the fix name. Cut for length: 'flight prior to event was uneventful'. Plain words used for 'green needles' (flight management system course guidance) and 'white needles' (localiser guidance). Judgement calls: the narratives differ slightly on the localiser sequence (one says navigation mode was armed before switching to localiser guidance, the other after); the first officer's order was used. Bracket 'descending' because the aircraft flew through the final approach course on the approach, where other approach traffic would be descending; no traffic is mentioned in the report.
